A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisJudge-Bench and VISJUDGE. All 53 pages of v1 and 62 pages of v2, including their appendices, support comparison. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection allowed matching of retained, relocated, and revised material.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, VISJUDGE fine-tuning results, training-data scaling experiments, and dataset analyses, including Table 3 and Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations across model backbones, downstream application results, and annotation-quality analyses in Table 3 and Appendices A.4 and E.

M1.justification: Section 4 extends VISJUDGE from a Qwen2.5-VL-7B model to variants using Qwen2.5-VL-3B, InternVL3-8B, and LLaVA-v1.6-mistral-7B. This broadens the model architectures while retaining the scoring outputs, GRPO/LoRA procedure, and accuracy-plus-format reward specified in Appendix D.

E1.justification: The original 3,090-image benchmark and its visualization categories remain. v2 adds visualization generation with iterative feedback through MatPlotAgent and visualization recommendation through HAIChart on VizML's user-created Plotly visualizations (Section 5.2.5 and Appendix E). These introduce distinct tasks and input distributions. New style/domain breakdowns characterize existing benchmark samples.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the seven original baselines and adds Qwen2.5-VL-3B/32B/72B-Instruct, InternVL3-8B, and LLaVA-v1.6-mistral-7B. The new downstream comparisons also evaluate original systems without VISJUDGE and alternatives using Qwen 7B or 72B feedback/reward models. Qwen-7B's expanded name is a naming clarification.

E3.justification: The original split, 648-sample benchmark evaluation, metrics, and training hyperparameters remain. Added experiments compare more model sizes and backbones under consistent training settings. Appendix E introduces GPT-4o assessment on a 0–100 scale for generated visualizations and Hit@1/Hit@3 for recommendation. Appendix B.6 introduces error-analysis subsets of 139 multiple visualizations and 94 dashboards.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the existing bias, complexity, case-study, and scaling analyses. Additions include backbone and downstream generalization tests, style/domain and coupled-design-failure analyses in Appendix A.2, annotation-quality audits in A.4, and quantified complex-visualization error patterns in B.6. Earlier illustrated cases are largely retained and renumbered.

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 newly quantifies annotation disagreement using crowd–crowd and crowd–expert MAE, including estimates by visualization type and annotator background. This adds statistical characterization of annotation noise. Both versions already average three model evaluations; v2 does not report increased repetitions, new seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises retained benchmark results: VISJUDGE's overall MAE/correlation changes from 0.442/0.681 to 0.421/0.687, GPT-5 from 0.551/0.429 to 0.553/0.428, and Qwen-7B's MAE from 1.048 to 0.847. Their revision's cause is unexplained. v2 also updates Figure 8's scaling results and adds backbone, annotation, and downstream results. Table 7 supports an average generation gain of 6.07 points, but its actual range is 4.10–8.91, contradicting the stated 5.53–8.91.

T1.justification: Appendix D retains the same exponential accuracy-reward equation and 0.9/0.1 reward weighting. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs. Updated empirical scaling fits and conceptual fidelity explanations do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a comprehensive visualization-quality benchmark, shortcomings of general MLLM judges, and improved human alignment through specialized training. Reported improvement percentages change, but these update supporting results without redefining those core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly limits fidelity assessment to visually detectable presentation problems when source data are unavailable, consistent with the retained appendix rubrics. It adds limitations concerning static visualizations, geographic concentration, subjective style categories, and small annotator subgroups. New interpretations attribute complex-chart failures to weak cross-view understanding and ineffective feedback to scoring biases; Appendix E also advances stronger generalization and production-readiness claims.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses 603 annotators and their geographic, professional, and educational composition. It documents consistent training configurations across four backbones and the downstream integration/evaluation procedures. Sections 7 and A.4 additionally promise annotations, quality-control records, statistical analyses, and model weights. Existing core hyperparameters, software information, and benchmark access link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations supporting style, domain, and dashboard analyses, including Bateman, Borkin, Sarikaya, and ChartGalaxy, plus references for newly evaluated model families. Section 2's research positioning and the benchmark's novelty claim remain essentially unchanged. Bibliographic updates and duplicate representations of existing works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify fidelity, condense annotation and case-study descriptions, and standardize model names. Appendix A is reorganized, the scaling subsection becomes Section 5.3, and limitations and extended-experiment sections are added. Much of the original prose and narrative sequence remains; the scientific additions do not amount to wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands into a substantially larger comparison organized by closed-source, open-source, and VISJUDGE groups. v2 adds application-result tables, with generation results displayed twice as Tables 4 and 7, and subtype boxplots in Figure 12. Figure 5 consolidates legends, Figure 8 changes plotting scales, and Figure 1 moves into the first page. Most appendix case illustrations remain.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens v1's single-backbone validation and previously unquantified annotator agreement through expanded Table 3, Appendix A.4, and two downstream applications in Appendix E. Clarifying visual-only fidelity also makes the evaluation scope more accurate. GPT-4o-based generation assessment, incomplete downstream settings, and the incorrect Table 7 gain range limit the stronger deployment claims, but the broader validation and annotation evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
